description: Shared Renovate preset for Corey Alan repos. Reference with: { "extends": ["github>Corey-Alan-Consulting/deploy-workflows:renovate-config"] }

hostRules.description: Read-only auth for restricted @corey-alan-consulting/* packages. NPM_READ_TOKEN is injected by the Renovate runner's secret store, never committed.

customManagers.description: BuildKit pin in setup-buildx-action driver-opts. Nothing else watches this: `driver-opts: image=moby/buildkit:<tag>` is not a dependency file, not an action ref and not a Dockerfile FROM, so every built-in manager skips it and the pin ages silently. #6's pin went three releases stale exactly this way, and #73's first cut was stale within twenty minutes of being written. Deliberately requires a numeric tag so the floating `buildx-stable-1` this pin exists to replace is never matched.

packageRules.description: Hand-curated security pins, not ordinary dependencies. In `overrides`, the KEY encodes the vulnerable range and the value is the patched floor, so Renovate reads the value as a plain range and offers the latest major — which forces that major on every transitive consumer matched by the key. On blue-skysolutions.com that turned `js-yaml@>=3.0.0 <3.15.0` into ^4.3.1, forcing @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config across the safeLoad API removal. Advisory bumps here have to be made by hand, against the advisory's own fix floor.

Third-party minor and patch updates arrive as ONE grouped, automergeable PR per repo rather than one PR per package. Placed before the first-party rule below so that rule still overrides groupName and minimumReleaseAge for @corey-alan-consulting/** — Renovate applies packageRules in order and later matches win. Why: on 2026-10-12 the fleet held 34 stale Renovate PRs and 223 open Dependabot alerts, 70 of them high or critical, runtime-scope and with a published fix. They were not ignored out of neglect; they were unmergeable with confidence, because no app PR gate compiled the app and green therefore meant 'types still check' rather than 'it still builds'. app-pr-checks v1.12.0 added that build step, which is what makes automerge here defensible at all. Majors are excluded: breaking by semver, so they keep opening individual PRs for review. Automerge assumes the consuming repo gates merges on required status checks, and it is NOT a release: the renovate-changeset workflow opens a separate changeset PR afterwards that a human still merges, so a dependency reaches production only by a deliberate act.

First-party packages: group + automerge minor/patch on green CI once a release has aged a day. Majors are breaking by semver, so they open a normal PR for human review. Automerge assumes the consuming repo gates merges on required status checks.
First-party reusable workflows / composite actions: bump the SHA pin when a new deploy-workflows release tag is cut; automerge non-major on green CI, same policy as internal packages.
Coordinate Auth.js bumps across repos while next-auth is still in beta.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes escape every throttle above: they ignore the weekly schedule, leave the non-major group so one unrelated failure cannot hold a CVE fix hostage, and skip minimumReleaseAge entirely — a three-day soak is prudent against a compromised release and indefensible against a known-exploited one. Deliberately does NOT set automerge. vulnerabilityAlerts is a separate config object rather than a packageRule, and it is not established that a consuming repo's blanket automerge:false packageRule reaches inside it — platform-infra relies on exactly such a rule to keep production infrastructure off automerge. A repo that wants security automerge can opt in locally, where the blast radius is visible.
